title: Philadelphia Fed December 2026 Livingston Survey — 10:00 a.m. ET on the funding-cliff date itself, the oldest continuous US forecaster survey landing on the calendar's most contested day
source: EST: philadelphiafed.org/calendar-of-events, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 131,096 bytes) — the Philadelphia Fed's own release calendar, whose embedded structured data carries exactly two Livingston rows for 2026, matching the survey's published semiannual June/December cadence: 'June Livingston Survey | Jun 24 2026 | 10:00 a.m.' and verbatim 'December Livingston Survey | Dec 11 2026 | 10:00 a.m.' Filed estimate on three counts: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no member for a regional Reserve Bank's own survey schedule (FED: covers the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar only), this lane never self-confirms an event it discovered in-sweep, and only the calendar row was read — no Livingston-specific release page was fetched. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of philly-fed-price-inflation-expectations-q4-2026-11-25, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED (not canonical) by the philly-fed-price-inflation-expectations-q4-2026-11-25 initial-research adjacency sweep on 2026-09-09, found in the same calendar payload that dated its proposer. Filed for the date collision, which is the whole of its interest: 2026-12-11 is already the calendar's most contested single day — cr-expiry-2026-12-11 (high, estimate), government-funding-deadline-2026-12-11 (high, estimate), russell-reconstitution-2026-12-11 (medium, estimate), ndx-annual-reconstitution-announcement-2026-12-11 (low, estimate) and sp-rebalance-reference-close-2026-12-11 (low, estimate) all sit on it — and this drops a Federal Reserve Bank publication into the middle of it. The Livingston Survey is the oldest continuously-published US forecaster survey (started 1946 by columnist Joseph Livingston, run by the Philadelphia Fed since 1990), semiannual, carrying six-month and twelve-month CPI and output forecasts. Two things make the collision worth a row rather than a footnote: it is Fed-funded and therefore publishes through an appropriations lapse where the BLS and Census prints around it do not (the premise philly-fed-mfg-2026-12-17 registers FT--1 against), and its June/December cadence means the December edition is the last professional forecast of the year, collected before the cliff resolves and published as it arrives. Impact LOW and symbols [] on the same grounds as every survey entry on this shelf: semiannual, low-frequency, no house playbook is macro-keyed, and no tracked name carries a forecaster-survey channel — the day's market relevance belongs to the cliff and the index events, not to this. Whoever writes the canonical file owns (a) re-verifying the date and time against a Livingston-specific release page rather than the shared calendar row, and (b) deciding whether a survey whose only claim is a shared date earns an entry at all — a DECLINE with the reasoning recorded would be a perfectly good outcome and is explicitly on the table. This is a PROPOSAL and an ESTIMATE — it widens caution, licenses nothing, and the proposing ledger registers no forward test that depends on it.
